findings.issue: Task 11 Step 3 instructs booting via './gradlew :backend:bootRun -PappArgs="-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full"' and the Acceptance Criteria + Verification Steps repeat this exact command. However, 'build.gradle' does NOT define a 'bootRun' task block that reads '-PappArgs' and passes values as JVM args. The Spring Boot Gradle plugin's 'bootRun' task does not honor '-PappArgs' out of the box — this flag has no effect. The correct Gradle flag to pass JVM arguments to bootRun is '-Pjvm.args' (if configured) or via the 'jvmArgs' property on the bootRun task, or by using '-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full' directly as a JVM flag with JAVA_OPTS or 'bootRun { jvmArgs = [...] }'. As-is, the command is a mirage: the JVM flag will be silently ignored and no pinning output will be captured.
findings.fix: Either: (a) add 'tasks.named("bootRun") { jvmArgs = project.findProperty("appArgs")?.split(" ") ?: [] }' to build.gradle, or (b) change the Verification Steps to use JAVA_OPTS: 'JAVA_OPTS="-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full" ./gradlew :backend:bootRun', or (c) use the Gradle toolchainJvmArgs mechanism. The task body and all AC/verification references must use the corrected command form.

findings.issue: Task 12 step 5 (AC18) says: 'Read MockHttpServletResponse.getCookies() (NOT the higher-level cookie().maxAge(...) matcher — that matcher only covers Max-Age and we need all attributes). Locate the SESSION cookie and assert: ... sameSite == "Strict" (read via Tomcat's Cookie API; if SameSite is not exposed there in the active Tomcat version, fall back to parsing the raw Set-Cookie header)'. The application.properties currently uses 'server.reactive.session.cookie.same-site=${SESSION_COOKIE_SAME_SITE:lax}' with a default value of 'lax' (not 'Strict'). The test-profile (application-test.properties) does NOT override SESSION_COOKIE_SAME_SITE. Therefore the test assertion 'SameSite=Strict' will fail in the test environment unless the environment variable SESSION_COOKIE_SAME_SITE is set to 'Strict'. The task assumes 'Strict' without verifying the test-profile value.
findings.fix: After Task 3 lands (which renames server.reactive to server.servlet), check application-test.properties for the actual cookie.same-site value. Either (a) set SESSION_COOKIE_SAME_SITE=Strict in application-test.properties and assert 'Strict', or (b) read the actual configured value dynamically in the test via @Value and assert whatever is configured. Do not hardcode 'Strict' unless the test profile actually sets it.

findings.issue: Task 10 Details section (item: ConcurrencyTestUtils.java) contains a full prescriptive implementation: 'try { ready.countDown(); start.await(); return task.call(); } finally { /* the countDown must reach zero unconditionally */ }'. The comment-block in the Details section then notes this exact code shape with precise method names, variable names, and the try/finally ordering. While framed as 'hints', this is a full algorithm with code logic — specifically the pattern 'ready.countDown() called inside try BEFORE task.call() AND the finally block is described as already fulfilling the contract'. Per checklist G, hints containing step-by-step algorithms or code blocks with full logic are severity major.
findings.fix: Reduce the Details/Implementation hints to conceptual pointers: 'Use CountDownLatch barrier with two latches (ready, start); ensure countDown is unconditional even on exception'. Remove the prescriptive try-block code shape from the Details section; the TDD Anchor tests provide the behavioral contract. The What-to-do section already describes the shape adequately.

findings.issue: Task 10 TDD Anchor's second test 'parallelInvoke_taskThrowingBeforeBarrier_doesNotHang' has a logical gap with the D10 contract. D10 mandates 'try { … } finally { ready.countDown(); }' — meaning ready.countDown() must happen BEFORE start.await() and task.call(). The Details section describes a different shape: 'ready.countDown(); start.await(); return task.call()' inside try — where ready.countDown() is the FIRST statement. In this shape, a task that throws AFTER ready.countDown() (i.e., in task.call()) would not hang ready.await() because countDown already happened. But a task that throws BEFORE ready.countDown() (e.g., in initialization code before countDown) WOULD hang. The test name says 'taskThrowingBeforeBarrier' — but the implementation hint places countDown as the first line, meaning nothing can throw before it. The test description is internally inconsistent with the hint about where countDown sits in the try block. One of them is misleading.
findings.fix: Align the test description with the actual barrier contract. If ready.countDown() is always the first statement, the test should be named 'parallelInvoke_taskThrowingDuringExecution_doesNotHang'. If the intent is to test a throw before ready.countDown(), the implementation must use try/finally wrapping countDown (not placing countDown first). Clarify which contract is correct.

findings.issue: Task 11 Step 4 instructs driving a 'synthetic register-storm' with curl: 'curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"email\":\"vt-probe-$i@example.com\",\"password\":\"Password123!\"}' but omits the CSRF token. After the Wave 2 migration, the app runs on the MVC servlet stack with CsrfFilter active on POST /api/auth/register. A bare curl POST will be rejected with 403 CSRF before reaching BCrypt. The pinning catalogue would then be empty for the register path — matching the Edge Cases note ('diagnose by checking response codes from the storm driver; if all 4xx, fix the request payload'). However the curl command in the Verification Steps does not mention obtaining a CSRF token first.
findings.fix: Add a pre-storm step to obtain an XSRF-TOKEN cookie (via GET /health or similar safe verb), then include it in the register-storm curl as '-H "X-XSRF-TOKEN: <value>" -b "XSRF-TOKEN=<value>"'. Alternatively note that for the VT-pinning probe, CSRF can be temporarily disabled in test configuration or a separate @SpringBootTest context can be used.
